technical_and_design_decisions: Treat the increment as changes to an existing Spring Cloud Data Flow/Stream ecosystem rather than as development of the Spring Framework itself.
Move the Kafka and Rabbit test rules and fixtures into independently buildable repositories, preserving their public test APIs and using versioned artifacts for consumption by other projects.
Expose platform-specific admin functionality through a common REST contract and adapt Lattice, YARN, and Cloud Foundry implementations behind that contract.
Represent registered libraries as first-class artifact metadata and resolve them when processing include and exclude statements.
Implement named channels as stream endpoints that can be referenced without requiring source and sink modules, while preserving existing stream deployment semantics.
Use the existing stream persistence and validation mechanisms to enforce stream-name uniqueness, including a database-level uniqueness constraint where supported.
Implement Kinesis source support using the existing source-module conventions and AWS SDK integration patterns.
Add automated controller tests at the API-contract level, using mocked services and repository fixtures where appropriate.
Preserve backward compatibility for existing APIs and configuration formats unless a user story explicitly requires a behavior change.
assumptions: The existing SCDF, Spring Cloud Stream, admin, persistence, build, and test infrastructure is available and builds successfully before the increment starts.
The developer has access to the existing source repositories, CI pipelines, artifact repositories, and required AWS/platform test credentials or suitable mocks.
The Kafka and Rabbit test-rule repositories require extraction, packaging, documentation, and CI setup, but not a redesign of their underlying test behavior.
The supported platform APIs and expected REST behavior for Lattice, YARN, and Cloud Foundry are sufficiently defined by existing implementations or established project conventions.

Kinesis source support is limited to the source module and its integration with the existing stream-module registration and deployment conventions; production-scale operational tooling is out of scope.
Testing can rely primarily on unit, mock-based integration, contract, and existing end-to-end test infrastructure rather than provisioning every target platform.
One workday represents one person-day of focused development effort, excluding elapsed waiting time for reviews or external environment availability.
Code review feedback, minor refactoring, and normal CI troubleshooting are included in the activity estimates.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing modules, APIs, persistence model, build layout, test conventions, and deployment integrations; define implementation boundaries and update plans for all eight user stories.

activities.activity_name: Extract Kafka test rule into a separate repository
activities.activity_description: Separate the Kafka rule and fixtures, create the repository build and publication configuration, preserve compatibility for consumers, migrate references, and add repository-level tests and CI.

activities.activity_name: Extract Rabbit test rule into a separate repository
activities.activity_description: Separate the Rabbit rule and fixtures, create the repository build and publication configuration, preserve compatibility for consumers, migrate references, and add repository-level tests and CI.

activities.activity_name: Provide consistent admin REST APIs across platforms
activities.activity_description: Define or normalize the common REST contract, implement platform-specific adapters for Lattice, YARN, and Cloud Foundry, update serialization and error handling, and add compatibility tests.

activities.activity_name: Support registered libraries in include and exclude statements
activities.activity_description: Extend artifact registration and metadata handling to identify libraries, update include/exclude resolution and validation, expose required API or CLI behavior, and test resolution and failure cases.

Add configuration, validation, persistence, deployment, and runtime handling for named channels so pipelines can be created without explicit source or sink modules, including backward-compatibility tests.

Create controller tests covering request validation, response payloads, status codes, error handling, and representative stream operations, using mocks and test fixtures to verify the public contract at build time.

Add service-level duplicate detection, persistence-level uniqueness enforcement where applicable, clear API errors, migration or compatibility handling, and tests for concurrent and repeated creation attempts.

Add the Kinesis source module using the project’s source conventions, configure AWS credentials and stream properties, implement message consumption and error handling, register metadata, and add unit and integration tests.

Run the complete build and relevant integration suites, verify interactions among registration, stream creation, named channels, REST APIs, and module support, diagnose regressions, and perform targeted fixes.

activities.activity_name: Documentation, release preparation, and final verification
activities.activity_description: Update user and developer documentation, migration and usage examples, release notes, dependency versions, repository publication configuration, and perform final quality and CI verification.
